transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… my family kind of wanted me to come, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I’ve just been having a hard time because they keep telling me the bank papers show nothing was taken, but I know what’s been going on.

It’s been over a year, and I really believe they’re hiding my money. They use things like bills, fundraisers, and even plans for trips to cover it up. I keep asking them about it because I just need them to tell the truth. I’m not trying to cause trouble or anything… I just don’t know what else to do.
Do you think your family is working together against you to hide your money?

I mean… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m accusing everybody just to be difficult. But yes, it feels like they’re all kind of going along with the same story.

They keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but I’ve known for over a year that my money is being hidden. And then there are all these bills, fundraisers, trip plans… it just feels like ways to cover it up. So I keep asking them, maybe more than they like, but I just need someone to tell me the truth.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be mistaken about your money being hidden?

I mean… I know you probably want me to say maybe, and I don’t want to sound stubborn. But I really don’t think I’m mistaken.

My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I’ve looked at what they show me, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it all feels like it’s being used to cover it up. So I keep bringing it up with them because I just need them to finally tell the truth.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about your money being hidden?

I mean… I don’t want to be difficult, Doctor. If somebody actually told the truth and showed me something real, I’d listen. But right now, no… I don’t really see how I could change my mind.

It’s been over a year, and I know they’re hiding my money. They keep pointing to the bank papers like that proves nothing was taken, but then there’s the bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it feels like that’s all part of covering it up. So I keep asking them about it, and I know they don’t like that, but I just need them to be honest with me.
Do you think your belief about your money being hidden could be a mistaken idea?

I… I know it probably sounds like I’m not being open-minded, and I’m trying to answer you the right way. But no, I don’t really think it’s just a mistaken idea.

I came in because my family and friends keep telling me the bank papers show nothing was taken, but I’ve known for over a year that my money is being hidden. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it all seems like part of covering it up. I don’t want to make trouble, but I feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally tell me the truth.
Do you think the people hiding your money are doing it in a way that's unusual or hard for others to understand?

I guess… maybe it sounds unusual when I say it out loud. I don’t want you to think I’m making wild accusations or anything.

But yes, it’s hard for other people to understand because they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. To me, it’s more than that. For over a year I’ve known my money is being hidden, and the bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it feels like those are being used to cover it up. That’s why I keep asking them, even if it upsets people. I just need them to finally tell the truth.
Do you think there's a specific plan or system that your family is using to hide your money?

I don’t know if I can explain it like a whole “system” the right way… I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing everybody of some big thing.

But yes, I think there is a plan. My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. And then the bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it feels like those are part of how they cover it up so it doesn’t look obvious.

I know that may sound bad, Doctor, but that’s why I keep confronting them. I just need them to tell the truth.
How much time would you say you spend thinking about your family hiding your money on a typical day?

I try not to think about it all day, Doctor… I really do. I don’t want to seem like I’m just sitting around obsessing over it.

But it comes up a lot. Like when bills come in, or somebody mentions a fundraiser, or trip plans, I start thinking about how that fits with them hiding my money. Some days it feels like it’s in the back of my mind most of the day, because I keep going over what they said and why the bank papers don’t show it.

I know maybe that sounds like too much… but I feel like if I stop paying attention, they’ll never tell me the truth.
Does thinking about your family hiding your money interfere with your daily activities?

Not really in the way people might think, Doctor. I mean… besides the arguments about the money, I still do what I’m supposed to do.

I make my own meals, I get myself to the county clinic and the assistance appointments, and I keep my things in order like I always have. So I don’t think I’m falling apart or anything. I know the money issue causes trouble, but I’m still handling my day-to-day things.
Do you think the way your family is hiding your money is something that could happen to anyone, or is it something very unusual?

I guess… I don’t think it’s something that happens to everyone, no. I know families have arguments about money, and maybe people hide things sometimes, but this feels more unusual because it’s been going on so long.

They keep pointing to the bank papers like that proves nothing happened, but I’ve known for over a year that my money is being hidden. And the bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… I’m sorry, I know it may sound like I’m making too much of it, but it feels like those things are being used to cover it up.

That’s why I keep confronting them. I just want them to tell the truth.
Do you think there is any evidence that could change your mind about your family hiding your money?

I mean… I want to say yes, because I don’t want you to think I’m unreasonable. If there was something that really explained all of it, maybe I’d try to listen.

But that’s the thing, Doctor… they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I know that’s what everyone wants me to accept. I just can’t, because I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it all feels like ways to cover it up.

So I don’t know what evidence would change my mind, honestly. I feel like until they tell me the truth, I have to keep asking and confronting them.
Do you think you will ever be able to stop thinking that your family is hiding your money?

I’d like to think I could, Doctor. I don’t want to be the kind of person who just keeps going over the same thing and upsetting everybody.

But… I don’t see how I can stop when I know it’s happening. My family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I know that’s what I’m supposed to accept, but for over a year I’ve felt sure they’re hiding my money. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… they all feel connected to it, like ways to cover it up.

So I guess unless they finally tell me the truth, I don’t know how I would stop thinking about it. I’ll try not to make it sound worse than it is, but I feel like I have to keep confronting them until they admit it.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think your family was hiding your money?

Not really… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’ve been stuck on it every single second, because I do try to go on with things.

But since my income dropped, about… a year and two months ago, that’s when I started feeling sure something was wrong with the money. Since then, I don’t think there’s really been a time where I fully didn’t think they were hiding it. Maybe I’ve tried to push it aside sometimes, but it’s still there.
Do you think the idea that your family is hiding your money is something that most people would consider strange or hard to believe?

I guess… yes, most people probably would think it sounds hard to believe. I know that’s why my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I understand how it might sound to someone else.

But to me it doesn’t feel strange. For over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it all feels like they’re using those things to cover it up. I don’t want to seem difficult, Doctor, but that’s why I keep confronting them. I feel like I have to until they tell the truth.
Do you think the idea that your family is hiding your money is something that could be considered a bizarre or unrealistic belief?

I mean… I can see how someone else might call it unrealistic, yes. I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

But to me it doesn’t feel bizarre. I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I know that’s what I’m supposed to believe, but for over a year I’ve felt sure they’re hiding my money. The bills and fundraisers and trip plans… they just feel like part of how they’re covering it up.

I know that may not sound right to you, Doctor, but I feel like I have to keep asking them about it until they tell the truth.
Do you think you could ever come to a point where you no longer believe your family is hiding your money?

I’d like to say yes, because I know that probably sounds like the healthier answer.

But honestly… I don’t know how I could stop believing it unless they admit what they did. I came in because everyone keeps telling me the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I understand that’s what you’re trying to help me look at. But for over a year I’ve felt sure they’re hiding my money.

The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… it all still feels connected, like a way to cover it up. So I keep thinking I have to confront them, maybe not in a bad way, but just until they finally tell the truth.
Has your belief that your family is hiding your money ever changed or wavered since it started?

Not really… I mean, I’ve tried to question it because I know that’s what everyone wants me to do. I don’t want to seem like I’m just being stubborn.

But since it started, it hasn’t really gone away. For over a year I’ve felt like they’re hiding my money, even though my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… they still feel like ways they’re covering it up.

So no, I guess it hasn’t really wavered much. I keep thinking if I confront them enough, they’ll finally tell the truth.
Do you think the idea that your family is hiding your money is a normal or ordinary concern?

I guess… no, not exactly normal. I know most people probably don’t worry their family is hiding money from them, and I don’t want you to think I’m trying to make trouble.

But it feels ordinary to me now because it’s been going on in my head for so long. For over a year I’ve felt sure they’re hiding my money, even though everyone keeps pointing to the bank papers and saying nothing was taken.

The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… I know maybe that sounds like I’m putting things together wrong, but to me it still feels like they’re using those things to cover it up. So I feel like I have to keep asking them, or confronting them, until they finally tell the truth.
Do you think there's any situation or evidence that could make you completely change your belief about your family hiding your money?

I want to say yes, because I know that’s what I’m supposed to be open to. And I did come here because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken.

But… honestly, I don’t know what evidence would change it completely. For over a year I’ve felt like I know they’re hiding my money. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans — it still feels like they’re using those things to cover it up.

Maybe if they actually sat down and told me the truth, then I could stop. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally admit it.

target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the belief has changed or wavered over time, which directly relates to the fixed, unchanging nature of the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
Not really… I mean, I’ve tried to question it because I know that’s what everyone wants me to do. I don’t want to seem like I’m just being stubborn.

But since it started, it hasn’t really gone away. For over a year I’ve felt like they’re hiding my money, even though my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… they still feel like ways they’re covering it up.

So no, I guess it hasn’t really wavered much. I keep thinking if I confront them enough, they’ll finally tell the truth.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of bizarre content in the delusion
doctor.question: Do you think the idea that your family is hiding your money is a normal or ordinary concern?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the belief about family hiding money is a normal concern or an unrealistic fixed belief, which directly relates to delusions.

patient.answer:
I guess… no, not exactly normal. I know most people probably don’t worry their family is hiding money from them, and I don’t want you to think I’m trying to make trouble.

But it feels ordinary to me now because it’s been going on in my head for so long. For over a year I’ve felt sure they’re hiding my money, even though everyone keeps pointing to the bank papers and saying nothing was taken.

The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans… I know maybe that sounds like I’m putting things together wrong, but to me it still feels like they’re using those things to cover it up. So I feel like I have to keep asking them, or confronting them, until they finally tell the truth.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of a fixed, unshakeable belief
doctor.question: Do you think there's any situation or evidence that could make you completely change your belief about your family hiding your money?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether any evidence could completely change the patient’s belief, which directly concerns the fixed and hard-to-change nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
I want to say yes, because I know that’s what I’m supposed to be open to. And I did come here because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken.

But… honestly, I don’t know what evidence would change it completely. For over a year I’ve felt like I know they’re hiding my money. The bills, the fundraisers, the trip plans — it still feels like they’re using those things to cover it up.

Maybe if they actually sat down and told me the truth, then I could stop. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just feel like I have to keep confronting them until they finally admit it.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent and unshakable belief that their family is hiding their money, despite evidence to the contrary, suggests a delusional disorder. The patient's belief is not necessarily bizarre, but it is a fixed, false belief that has been present for over a year.
